digest.component_or_area: Gerrit Verify CI pipeline - Ubuntu job optimization
propositions: Ubuntu Verify jobs occupy 30+ runner-minutes per change due to repeated YAML parsing in bridge cadence test (1,440 iterations) and redundant Pandoc corpus subprocess execution (3,421 processes across 884 units with legacy oracle duplication).

Bridge cadence test parse cost is 7.653s with I/O versus 0.001s when schedule is loaded once; hoisting YAML load from within the 1,440-minute comprehension to setup phase eliminates 342s per Verify run while preserving exhaustive arithmetic proof.

Pandoc hardening oracle executes both live and legacy conversion for all 884 units but asserts only existence; replacing legacy side with static immutable baseline while keeping all 884 live conversions removes 883 redundant subprocesses and preserves ADR 0095 compliance.

GitHub workflow cancellation uses always() status checks that evaluate true on superseded patchsets, preventing job cancellation and causing 25m admission delays; replacing with !cancelled() restores cancellation while preserving classifier-failure full fallback.

Post-remediation organic runs show end-to-end completion in 22-26 minutes with no individual pytest phase exceeding 30s, meeting the 20-30 minute target; Ubuntu occupancy reduced 21.1% (436s freed per run) without losing coverage or adding parallel jobs.

Proposed full-substitution of corpus real-Pandoc with static golden fixtures requires ADR 0095 supersession; architecturally sound by OSS consensus but blocked pending operator approval; alternative bounded live-probe plus weekly full replay in External Integration preserves all assertion classes with lower adoption risk.
